rounds.prompt: A goldfish critic doing avenCEO's Review gate (g-6de7) on aip-59ad's checkpoint 2, read-only: no push, GitHub, SSH or fetch of aven.maia.city, no docker or check command; test.sh without --box allowed. Read aip-59ad (c3, c4, c5, checkpoint 2, assumptions, deferred, events, problem.evidence) and the Review gate; rv-d660 is settled; the server as the legacy files describe it (avendeploy.yml, caddy.sh, the Caddyfile's aven.maia.city block). Review commit 7eea72eff: theos.yml's deploy job, theOS/release/deploy.sh, undo.sh, ssh.sh, health.sh, test.sh. Questions: do the work and its tests keep c3, c4, c5; will the deploy work against the server as described (paths, the deploy user's rights, the link through /srv/site, relative targets, what caddy.sh left); can it write outside releases and the two links, touch the peer or Caddy, or leave the site half-switched; is health.sh's comparison sound (compression, redirects, caching, certificate, DNS); is the undo sound after several deploys; can the key leak; what breaks on the first real run; what is unproven before Gate B. Findings with severity, kind, file and line, reasoning, fix, evidence; at most 500 words.

findings.text: Every push to production runs deploy.sh, which switches whenever current is not the commit's tree, so after an undo the next push that does not touch theOS/ puts the undone build back.
findings.note: The switch step skips the deploy when the tree before the push (github.event.before, fetched) equals the commit's; test.sh asserts the step reads it.

findings.text: undo.sh never reaches the server and nothing runs it; undo goes one step deep, so after two deploys no command reaches avenOS; and once this is on production the first merge is the first real deploy, not Gate B's.
findings.note: A workflow, theOS undo (.github/workflows/theos-undo.yml), run by hand in the environment production, copies undo.sh and runs it; undo.sh takes a build by name (26.10.31v6 is avenOS), tested after two deploys and for a missing name; the deploy also copies undo.sh. The deploy is off until Gate B: theOS/release/deploy.on holds off, and every deploy step needs it on (test.sh asserts the switch, and that no step before it reads a secret).

findings.text: bash -e without pipefail: a failed deploy.sh shows green.
findings.note: shell: bash (pipefail) on the piped steps; test.sh asserts it (tried by a mutation).
